reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that SiC addition to a different HEA (CoCrFeNi) via arc melting forms in-situ carbides and silicides, dramatically increasing yield strength while retaining ductility. However, it does not address the specific (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 system, its caloric response, or the claim that crack deflection/bridging by SiC nanoparticles will yield a ≥50% compressive strength increase without degrading caloric performance. The key premises about caloric retention and the specific mechanical improvement in this alloy are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: SiC addition to HEAs can be achieved via arc melting, forming in-situ carbides/silicides that enhance strength
Uniform dispersion of hard phases in an HEA matrix improves mechanical properties without catastrophic embrittlement
The caloric response in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 relies on lattice instabilities that can be preserved if no deleterious phases form
A small volume fraction of ceramic nanoparticles can deflect and bridge cracks, increasing compressive strength by ≥50%
Optimized melting and annealing can suppress adverse reactions between SiC and the specific HEA constituents
